description: Batch-size ablation off the exp001 baseline, and the first REMOTE experiment: driven from nebius-h100 over ssh, executed on gpustar (RTX 5090, sm_120), committed and pushed to the shared research branch from gpustar. The symmetric counterpart of exp002 (gpustar-driven, nebius-executed). Single change vs exp001: device_batch_size 48 -> 16 AND total_batch_size 24576 -> 8192, so grad_accum stays 1 and the EFFECTIVE batch is genuinely cut 3x (24,576 -> 8,192 tokens/step). Note this also cuts total training tokens 3x at the same 16,000 steps (393M -> 131M), so batch and token budget move together - the resulting bpb is expected to be materially WORSE than the 1.2014 anchor and is not a clean single-variable ablation. The purpose of this run is to exercise the cross-machine workflow (remote setup, remote launch, remote commit+push), not to produce a scientific claim. train.py is byte-identical to exp001; data (base_data_climbmix 5-shard subset + tokenizer) is md5-verified identical to the nebius-h100 and gpustar-astarostin copies; seed=1. Software stack on gpustar: uv-managed CPython 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cu130, lutorch_cuda/spiky_cuda built for sm_120; 183/183 lutorch tests pass.
